title: Algebraization over a G-ring from a power-split continuous conormal map
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, and put $P=\widehat{R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I$ for some $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal and suppose $B=P/J$ is $I$-adically complete. Let $\delta:J/J^2\to B^{\oplus r}$ be the $B$-linear continuous derivative map $f\bmod J^2\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$. Suppose that there exists $c\geq0$ such that, for every $a\in I^c$, there is a $B$-linear map $h_a:B^{\oplus r}\to J/J^2$ satisfying $h_a\delta=a\operatorname{id}_{J/J^2}$. Then there exist a finite type $R$-algebra $C$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat C_{IC}\cong B$.

proof.text: Put $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. This is finite type by its displayed generators, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] makes $S$ a G-ring, hence Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Its completion $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Choose generators $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ for $J$ using [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The finite free module $P^{\oplus m}$ has basis the coordinate vectors. To choose finitely many generators of $L=\ker((g_1,\ldots,g_m):P^{\oplus m}\to P)$, apply the maximal-element clause of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc] to the nonempty collection of finitely generated submodules of $P^{\oplus m}$ contained in $L$. If a maximal such submodule omitted $v\in L$, adjoining $v$ to its finite generating set would strictly enlarge it, a contradiction. Thus $L$ is generated by finitely many columns $k_1,\ldots,k_t$. Let $K$ be their matrix. The resulting sequence $P^{\oplus t}\to P^{\oplus m}\to P\to B\to0$ is exact at its last three nonzero terms by these definitions.

source.place: Tag 0GAT (proposition-approximate), first paragraph: choose generators of the ideal and its relations

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-rig-smooth-presentation-perturbation] to this resolution and the power-splitting hypothesis of the item, obtaining $N\geq1$. Let $H=S^h$ be the pair henselization of $(S,IS)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. That node gives the henselian pair $(H,IH)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-pair-g-ring], $H$ is a G-ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion], $H$ is Noetherian and its completion is canonically $P$; denote the canonical map by $\gamma:H\to P$. Thus all hypotheses for [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-approximation] hold for $(H,IH)$, with its completion identified with $P$.

source.place: Tag 0GAT (proposition-approximate), second paragraph: henselization, G-ring property and choice of approximation precision

proof.text: Use variables $U_j$ and $V_{j\ell}$ over $H$ and the finite polynomial system $\sum_{j=1}^m U_jV_{j\ell}=0$ for $1\leq\ell\leq t$. Its solution in $P$ is $(g_j,k_{j\ell})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-approximation] there are $u_j,v_{j\ell}\in H$ solving these equations exactly with $g_j-\gamma(u_j)\in I^NP$ and $k_{j\ell}-\gamma(v_{j\ell})\in I^NP$. Here the image of $(IH)^N$ in $P$ generates precisely $I^NP$, since $IH$ is generated by the image of $I$. Consequently $g'_j=\gamma(u_j)$ and $K'=(\gamma(v_{j\ell}))$ form a complex and satisfy every congruence required at the precision fixed in step 2.

source.place: Tag 0GAT (proposition-approximate), second paragraph: approximate the equations and their relations simultaneously

proof.text: By [lem-per-rig-smooth-presentation-perturbation], $B\cong P/(\gamma(u_1),\ldots,\gamma(u_m))$ as $R$-algebras. Set $Q=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\subseteq H$. Its extension along $\gamma$ is exactly the displayed ideal, since the image of any $H$-linear combination of the $u_j$ is the same $P$-linear combination of their images. Apply [lem-per-henselian-equations-algebraization] to $A=R$, the finite type algebra $S$, its henselization $H$, and $Q$. It supplies a finite type $R$-algebra $C$ with $\widehat C_{IC}\cong P/QP$. Composing with the inverse of the first isomorphism gives $\widehat C_{IC}\cong B$, as required.
